title: Dashboard design decision log and trace rules
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures design questions, short decision records, and practical tracing rules for upcoming inference dashboards. Goal: move fast on a minimal, operator-friendly dashboard surface for model rollouts and SLO investigation while keeping query cost and trace volume bounded.

Why this doc exists (quick):
- Reduce rework: record trade-offs and the small set of metric semantics we agreed on.
- Reduce operator confusion: canonicalize span names and enrichment keys for cross-team traces.
- Cost guardrails: explicit sampling/aggregation rules so panels don't blow query budgets.

Scope (what this is for):
- Live rollouts (canary/capacity fallbacks) dashboards and investigation panels.
- Token-path latency attribution, cache-warmth signals, and model-fallback traces.
- Not covering billing dashboards (finance) or deep model quality eval dashboards (research). Those remain separate.

Decision log (chronological, short):
- 2025-01-15: Use session_id + request_id as primary stitch keys for dashboard panels and trace joins. Why: gives an efficient way to join traces with panel rows for slow requests. Owner: Liam C.
- 2025-01-20: Default trace sampling at 0.5% for steady traffic, bumped to 5% for request latency > p95. Why: default keeps storage/cost in check while surface-area for tail analysis remains useful. Owner: Aisha P.
- 2025-01-22: Represent KV-cache warmness as two signals: kv_cache_hit_rate (last-minute window) and kv_cache_warmth_index (session-level heuristic). Panel uses both. Why: hit_rate is stable; warmth index surfaces cross-tenant cold-starts. Owner: Ravi K.
- 2025-01-27: Dashboard panels will prioritize quantile views (p50,p90,p95,p99) over mean for latency. Why: token-serving latencies are heavy-tailed. Owner: Sofia M.
- 2025-02-03: Limit per-panel query window to 30m by default with a dropdown to increase to 6h. Why: default reduces accidental high-cost queries. Owner: Noah R.

Metric definitions (canonical list):
- request.count: total number of inference requests received. unit: count. ingestion: per-request increment. owner: eng-serving-runtime. alert baseline: drop of >15% vs 1h baseline.
- token.generated_per_request.avg: average output tokens per request (rolling 5m). unit: tokens/request. owner: product-hosted-api. use-case: normalizing cost SLOs.
- latency.server_p95_ms: 95th percentile server processing time (end-to-end excluding client network). unit: ms. window: rolling 5m. owner: eng-serving-runtime. alert: p95 > 250ms for >5m.
- latency.kv_cache_lookup_ms.p95: time spent in KV cache lookups. unit: ms. note split by tenant/model. owner: eng-platform.
- kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of prefix/KV hits across token predictions in a minute. unit: 0..1. owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- model.fallback_rate: fraction of requests routed to lower-tier model variant (e.g., quantized). unit: 0..1. owner: routing-team. alert: sudden >3x increase.
- session.warmth_index: heuristic 0..100 indicating how primed a session is (uses prefix length, previous requests). owner: eng-observability.
- request.error_rate: fraction of requests with non-2xx or internal error classification. unit: 0..1. alert: >1% sustained.

Tracing rules (practical):
- Span naming conventions:
  - span:request_handler -> instrument entry point; attributes: request_id, session_id, tenant_id, model_variant, route
  - span:model_infer -> encloses the model runtime invocation; add attributes: model_name, seq_len, kv_cache_hit (bool), batch_size
  - span:kv_lookup -> for KV cache calls; attributes: key_count, hit_count, lookup_ms
  - span:rpc_* for downstream infra calls (storage, auth). Keep names stable for grouping.
- Minimum attributes to attach to root span: request_id, session_id, tenant_id, route, model_variant, priority_tier. No PII fields.
- Redaction: drop any prompt/user content in traces. If prompt hashes are needed, only attach a SHA256 prefix (8 chars) and store mapping in a locked Confluence page for authorized teams.
- Sampling policy (operational):
  - steady-state: 0.5% of requests sampled globally.
  - tail-elevation: auto-sample any request with latency > p95 for sampling-window of 10m at 100% until tail event resolves.
  - error-capture: sample all requests with request.error_rate flags (all errors).
  - canary-high: for traffic flagged as canary rollout, sample at 10% by default.
- Trace retention tiers: short (7d high-res), long (30d aggregated traces with only root/timing attributes).

Dashboard panel sketches (operator-first):
- Panel: Rollout health (top row)
  - widgets: request.count (timeseries), model.fallback_rate (timeseries), request.error_rate (heatmap by tenant)
  - intent: immediate triage: is traffic dropping? are fallbacks increasing? where errors concentrated?
- Panel: Latency decomposition (middle row)
  - widgets: latency.server_p95_ms (quantiles), stacked bars for kv_lookup vs model_infer vs rpc overhead (derived from span durations), table showing top 10 tenants by p95 delta
  - intent: quickly find whether latency is model or infra bound.
- Panel: Cache warmth & cold-start indicators
  - widgets: kv_cache_hit_rate (per-model), session.warmth_index distribution, scatter of seq_len vs warmth
  - intent: identify low-warmth cohorts causing token surges.
- Panel: Trace sampling heatmap (ops)
  - widgets: sampled traces count, sample rate overrides active (list), recent sampled traces links (last 50)
  - note: always show link + request_id to trace viewer.

Query cost & budget guardrails:
- Default per-dashboard query budget: 5000 query units/day per team owning the dashboard. Dashboard templates must include estimated QUs.
- Aggregation rules: use pre-aggregated buckets where possible (minute-level rollups) and avoid raw log scans in panels.
- Recommendation: for high-cardinality tables (tenant/model), show top-k and provide drill-in links instead of full cardinality overviews.

Operational play snippets (how to use during incidents):
- If p95 jumps: open Rollout health -> check model.fallback_rate and kv_cache_hit_rate. If fallback_rate rising with kv_hit_rate falling, suspect model infra/degradation or KV eviction.
- If errors spike without latency shift: check recent deploys (linked PRs) and route-level configs; search sampled error traces for exception types and auth/rate-limit spans.

Unresolved questions / trade-offs (open items):
- Exact warmth_index formula: currently prototype uses weighted last-5 requests + avg prefix length; need product validation (owner: Ravi).
- How aggressively to redact prompt metadata vs usefulness for RLHF teams (owner: security + ML research).
- Should per-tenant quotas surface on the same dashboard or live in a separate tenant-management view? (owner: product-hosted-api).

Action items (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint A (by 2025-02-09): implement sampling toggles and tail-elevation hooks. Owner: Aisha P.
- Sprint B (by 2025-02-23): wire basic Rollout Health dashboard template using minute rollups + precomputed quantiles. Owner: Noah R.
- Sprint C (by 2025-03-10): finalize metric contract docs for kv_cache_hit_rate and session.warmth_index; add unit tests for metric derivations. Owner: Ravi K.

Notes to readers (style):
- This is a working record: use the Decision log section to record any changes. Keep entries brief and date them.
- When adding a new metric, include: name, owner, ingestion pattern, cardinality guidance, and a one-line rationale.

Appendix (useful snippets):
- Suggested attribution query (psuedocode):
  SELECT quantile(0.95)(duration_ms) AS p95, sum(kv_lookup_ms) AS kv_sum, sum(model_infer_ms) AS model_sum
  WHERE time > now() - 5m
  GROUP BY tenant_id, model_name
- Safe trace attribute set: [request_id, session_id, tenant_id, model_name, model_variant, route, seq_len, batch_size]

End of doc.
